Removed cc Prithvi Pai <prithvi24pai@gmail.com>.

Nice! Good cleanup. I was wondering why the order of DIMM was shuffled around on my system to be different from their names. I wouldn't mind this being the default behavior, but that would be a breaking change, so probably best to leave it as-is.

Conceptual question. What happens if there is more than one object at the same path? With the old way of allocating numbers in sequence, this was impossible. However, with this new way of allocating numbers based on the detected content, it is conceivable that an untrustworthy or buggy SMBIOS table could create more than one DIMM object with exactly the same number. Would this cause the D-Bus call to error out and thus not create the object?
(didn't mean to mark this as Resolved)

This would mean in issue in the BIOS which would have to be fixed separately.

```
 Would this cause the D-Bus call to error out and thus not create the object?
```
Yes

This might be a case for platforms currently using this smbios daemon but this is why I made it an opt-in feature so that existing platforms would not break even if this were the case.

OK, good. It won't crash or do other bothersome behavior if a duplicate object is detected, I'm assuming? It's OK to simply drop the duplicate object and not create it, since as you said, that indicates a bug in the underlying BIOS. I was just concerned about a doubled-up object or weird crash happening.
Nice, this is a good cleanup. Someone in the future should also do this for CPU and PCIe objects.
Good to see such improvement, but suggest to attach all the modification into this gerrit commit as normal which will be better to review and commit comments.
